units.zh: 中國自書契以來，以禮教治天下。
units.en: Since the age of written contracts, China has governed the realm through ritual instruction.
units.literal: From the age of written contracts onward, China has governed All-under-Heaven through ritual instruction.

units.zh: 勞之來之而政出焉，匡之直之而刑生焉。
units.en: By comforting and calling the people forth, government emerged; by correcting and straightening them, punishments arose.
units.literal: When one comforts and summons them, government emerges; when one corrects and straightens them, punishments arise.

units.zh: 政也，刑也，凡皆以維持禮教於勿替。
units.en: Government and punishments alike all served to uphold ritual instruction without decline.
units.literal: Government and punishments alike—all were to maintain ritual instruction without replacement.

units.zh: 故尚書曰：「明於五刑，以弼五教。」
units.en: Hence the Book of Documents says: "Be clear about the five punishments, to assist the five teachings."
units.literal: Hence the Book of Documents says: "Be clear about the five punishments, to assist the five teachings."

units.zh: 又曰：「士制百姓於刑之中，以教祗德。」
units.en: It also says: "The minister established the people within the norms of punishment, to teach reverent virtue."
units.literal: It also says: "The minister established the common people within the norms of punishment, to teach reverent virtue."

units.zh: 古先哲王，其制刑之精義如此。
units.en: Such was the essential meaning of how the ancient sage kings fashioned punishments.
units.literal: The essential meaning of the ancient sage kings' establishment of punishments was thus.

units.zh: 周衰禮廢，典籍散失。
units.en: When the Zhou declined, ritual was abandoned and the classical records were scattered and lost.
units.literal: When Zhou declined, ritual was abandoned, and the classical records were scattered and lost.

units.zh: 魏李悝著法經六篇，流衍至於漢初，蕭何加為九章，歷代頗有增損分合。
units.en: Li Kui of Wei wrote the six chapters of the Classic of Law, which passed down to early Han when Xiao He expanded them into the Nine Chapters; successive dynasties then added, cut, divided, and merged them in various ways.
units.literal: Li Kui of Wei composed the six chapters of the Classic of Law; it flowed down to early Han, when Xiao He expanded it into the Nine Chapters; through successive dynasties there was considerable addition, subtraction, division, and merger.

units.zh: 至唐永徽律出，始集其成。
units.en: When the Tang Yonghui Code appeared, the legal corpus was first fully assembled.
units.literal: When the Yonghui Code of Tang appeared, the corpus was first fully gathered.

units.zh: 雖沿宋迄元、明而面目一變，然科條所布，於扶翼世教之意，未嘗不兢兢焉。
units.en: Though from Song through Yuan and Ming its form changed entirely, the statutes promulgated never ceased to pursue, with scrupulous care, the aim of supporting the moral instruction of the age.
units.literal: Although from Song through Yuan and Ming its aspect changed entirely, in the statutes promulgated the intent to support the teachings of the age was never absent—always pursued with care.

units.zh: 君子上下數千年間，觀其教化之昏明，與夫刑罰之中不中，而盛衰治亂之故，綦可睹矣。
units.en: Over several thousand years, the discerning observer can plainly see the causes of rise and fall, order and chaos, by watching whether moral instruction was enlightened or benighted and whether punishments were measured or excessive.
units.literal: Over several thousand years above and below, gentlemen observing whether instruction was dark or bright, and whether punishments were fitting or unfitting, can plainly see the causes of prosperity and decline, order and disorder.

units.zh: 有清起自遼左，不三四十年混一區宇。
units.en: The Qing arose in eastern Liao; within three or four decades they unified the realm.
units.literal: The Qing arose from the eastern Liao region; in barely three or four decades they unified the realm.

units.zh: 聖祖沖年踐阼，與天下休養，六十餘稔，寬恤之詔，歲不絕書。
units.en: The Sacred Ancestor came to the throne in his youth and gave the realm its repose; for more than sixty years, edicts of clemency and relief were issued without cease.
units.literal: The Sacred Ancestor ascended the throne in his minority and rested the realm in peace with All-under-Heaven; for more than sixty years, edicts of clemency and relief were issued without cease year after year.

units.zh: 高宗運際昌明，一代法制，多所裁定。
units.en: When Gaozong's reign coincided with a flourishing age, many of the legal institutions of that generation were definitively settled.
units.literal: When Gaozong's fortune coincided with a glorious age, the legal institutions of that generation were largely settled.

units.zh: 仁宗以降，事多因循，未遑改作。
units.en: From Renzong onward, affairs were largely left to inertia, without time to undertake reform.
units.literal: From Renzong onward, affairs were largely pursued by inertia, without leisure to reform.

units.zh: 綜其終始，列朝刑政，雖不盡清明，然如明代之廠衛、廷杖，專意戮辱士大夫，無有也。
units.en: Taken as a whole from beginning to end, the penal administration of successive reigns was not wholly lucid, yet nothing like the Ming practice of the Factory Guards and court beating, devoted to humiliating and killing scholar-officials, ever appeared.
units.literal: Taking their course from beginning to end, the penal administration of successive reigns, though not entirely lucid and clear, yet such things as the Ming dynasty's Factory Guards and court beating, devoted to humiliating and killing scholar-officials, did not exist.

units.zh: 治獄者雖不盡仁恕，然如漢、唐之張湯、趙禹、周興、來俊臣輩，深文慘刻，無有也。
units.en: Those who ran the prisons were not always humane, yet there were none like Zhang Tang and Zhao Yu of Han or Zhou Xing and Lai Junchen of Tang, who twisted the law into cruel severity.
units.literal: Those who administered prisons were not entirely humane and forgiving, yet such men as Zhang Tang and Zhao Yu of Han and Zhou Xing and Lai Junchen of Tang, who twisted the law cruelly and severally—none such existed.

units.zh: 德宗末葉，庚子拳匪之變，創巨痛深，朝野上下，爭言變法，於是新律萌芽。
units.en: In Dezong's final years, after the catastrophe of the 1900 Boxer uprising, with wounds still fresh and pain still deep, court and country alike clamored for reform, and the new penal code began to take shape.
units.literal: In the closing years of Dezong, at the upheaval of the Boxer year 1900, with wounds fresh and pain deep, court and country alike clamored for reform, and thus the new penal code began to sprout.

units.zh: 迨宣統遜位，而中國數千年相傳之刑典俱廢。
units.en: When Xuantong abdicated, the penal codes that China had transmitted for thousands of years were all abolished.
units.literal: By the time Xuantong abdicated, the penal codes handed down in China for thousands of years were all abolished.

units.zh: 是故論有清一代之刑法，亦古今絕續之交也。
units.en: Thus in treating Qing penal law as a whole, one stands at the very juncture where ancient and modern legal continuity was severed.
units.literal: Therefore in discussing Qing dynasty penal law as a whole, it stands also at the juncture where ancient and modern continuity was severed.

units.zh: 爰備志之，俾後有考焉。
units.en: Accordingly it is set down here in full, that posterity may have material for study.
units.literal: Accordingly this is recorded in full in the treatise, that posterity may have material for inquiry.

units.zh: 清太祖嗣服之初，始定國政，禁悖亂，戢盜賊，法制以立。
units.en: At the outset of his succession, Qing Taizu first settled state affairs, forbade rebellion and disorder, suppressed banditry, and thereby established the legal order.
units.literal: At the outset when Qing Taizu succeeded to the inheritance, he first settled state affairs, forbade rebellion and disorder, quelled bandits, and thereby established legal institutions.

units.zh: 太宗繼武，於天聰七年，遣國舅阿什達爾漢等往外籓蒙古諸國宣布欽定法令，時所謂「盛京定例」是也。
units.en: Taizong continued the martial tradition; in the seventh year of Tiancong he sent his maternal uncle Ashi Darhan and others to the outer Mongol states to proclaim the imperially ordained statutes—what was then known as the "Shengjing Established Precedents."
units.literal: Taizong continued the martial endeavor; in the seventh year of Tiancong he dispatched his maternal uncle Ashi Darhan and others to the outer Mongol states to proclaim the imperially ordained statutes—what was then called the "Shengjing Established Precedents."

units.zh: 嗣復陸續著有治罪條文，然皆因時立制，不盡垂諸久遠。
units.en: Penal provisions were compiled one after another, but all were measures for the moment and were not meant to endure for the long term.
units.literal: Subsequently penal provisions were continually compiled, but all were measures for the moment, not entirely intended to endure.

units.zh: 世祖順治元年，攝政睿親王入關定亂，六月，即令問刑衙門准依明律治罪。
units.en: In Shunzhi 1, while the regent Prince Rui was entering the passes to quell disorder, in the sixth month he ordered the judicial yamen to adjudicate crimes according to the Ming Code.
units.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi under Shizu, the regent Prince Rui entered the passes to settle disorder; in the sixth month he at once ordered the judicial yamen to adjudicate crimes according to the Ming Code.

units.zh: 八月，刑科給事中孫襄陳刑法四事，一曰定刑書：「刑之有律，猶物之有規矩準繩也。
units.en: In the eighth month, Criminal Affairs supervising secretary Sun Xiang submitted four proposals on penal law. The first was to fix the penal code: "Law in penal matters is to things what compass and square are to measurement.
units.literal: In the eighth month, Criminal Affairs supervising secretary Sun Xiang submitted four matters on penal law, the first being to fix the penal text: "To have law in penal matters is like having compass and square for things.

units.zh: 今法司所遵及故明律令，科條繁簡，情法輕重，當稽往憲，合時宜，斟酌損益，刊定成書，布告中外，俾知畫一遵守，庶奸慝不形，風俗移易。」
units.en: The statutes now followed by the judicial offices and the former Ming codes vary in complexity and in how circumstance and law weigh light or heavy. These should be checked against past statutes, fitted to present needs, carefully revised, engraved as a fixed book, and promulgated at home and abroad so that all may observe a single standard; then wickedness may not take shape and customs may change for the better."
units.literal: The statutes now followed by the judicial offices and the old Ming codes and ordinances—whether articles are numerous or few, whether circumstances and law are light or heavy—should be examined against past statutes, fitted to present needs, weighed for addition and subtraction, engraved and fixed as a book, promulgated within and without, so that all may know and uniformly observe; then wickedness may not take form and customs may change."

units.zh: 疏上，攝政王諭令法司會同廷臣詳繹明律，參酌時宜，集議允當，以便裁定成書，頒行天下。
units.en: When the memorial was submitted, the regent ordered the judicial offices, together with court ministers, to expound the Ming Code in detail, weigh present needs, deliberate until agreement was reached, and then fix the code as a book to be promulgated throughout the realm.
units.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the regent ordered the judicial offices together with court ministers to expound the Ming Code in detail, weigh present needs, assemble discussion until satisfactory, and thereby fix and promulgate the book throughout the realm.

units.zh: 十月，世祖入京，即皇帝位。
units.en: In the tenth month Shizu entered the capital and assumed the throne.
units.literal: In the tenth month Shizu entered the capital and at once assumed the imperial throne.

units.zh: 刑部左侍郎黨崇雅奏，在外官吏，乘茲新制未定，不無憑臆舞文之弊。
units.en: Left vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments Dang Chongya memorialized that local officials, taking advantage of the unsettled new system, were not above twisting the law to suit their whims.
units.literal: Left vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments Dang Chongya memorialized that local officials, taking advantage of the fact that the new system was not yet fixed, were not without the abuse of twisting the text according to whim.

units.zh: 並乞暫用明律，候國制畫一，永垂令甲。
units.en: He also asked that the Ming Code be used temporarily until the national system was unified and could be handed down as permanent law.
units.literal: He also requested that the Ming Code be used temporarily, until the national system was unified and might be handed down forever as binding ordinance.

units.zh: 得旨：「在外仍照明律行，如有恣意輕重等弊，指參重處。」
units.en: The rescript read: "Outside the capital, continue to follow the Ming Code. If officials arbitrarily vary punishments in severity, report them for severe punishment."
units.literal: An imperial rescript was received: "Outside the capital, continue to act according to the Ming Code; if there are abuses such as arbitrary lightness or heaviness, report and refer for severe punishment."

units.zh: 二年，命修律官參稽滿、漢條例，分輕重等差，從刑科都給事中李士焜請也。
units.en: In the second year he ordered the code-revising officials to examine Manchu and Han regulations and distinguish grades of severity, following a request from Criminal Affairs chief supervising secretary Li Shikun.
units.literal: In the second year he ordered the officials revising the code to examine Manchu and Han regulations and distinguish grades of lightness and heaviness, following the request of Criminal Affairs chief supervising secretary Li Shikun.

units.zh: 三年五月，大清律成，世祖御制序文曰：「朕惟太祖、太宗創業東方，民淳法簡，大辟之外，惟有鞭笞。
units.en: In the fifth month of the third year the Great Qing Code was completed. Shizu wrote a preface in his own hand: "I reflect that Taizu and Taizong founded the enterprise in the east, where the people were simple and the law was spare—apart from capital punishment there was only flogging.
units.literal: In the fifth month of the third year the Great Qing Code was completed; Shizu composed a preface in his own hand, saying: "I consider that Taizu and Taizong founded the enterprise in the east; the people were simple and the law was spare—apart from capital punishment there was only flogging.

units.zh: 朕仰荷天休，撫臨中夏，人民既眾，情偽多端。
units.en: I, bearing Heaven's favor, now rule central China; the people are numerous, and truth and falsehood take many forms.
units.literal: I, bearing Heaven's favor, rule over central China; the people are already numerous, and truth and falsehood take many forms.

units.zh: 每遇奏讞，輕重出入，頗煩擬議。
units.en: Whenever cases came up for judgment, punishments varied inconsistently in severity, and deliberation became burdensome.
units.literal: Whenever cases were reported for judgment, lightness and heaviness varied, and deliberation was quite troublesome.

units.zh: 律例未定，有司無所稟承。
units.en: With statutes and precedents still unfixed, officials had no authority to follow.
units.literal: With statutes and precedents unfixed, the responsible officials had nothing to receive and follow.

units.zh: 爰敕法司官廣集廷議，詳譯明律，參以國制，增損劑量，期於平允。
units.en: Therefore I charged the judicial offices to gather broad court discussion, translate the Ming Code in detail, consult our national institutions, revise it with care, and aim at fairness.
units.literal: Therefore I charged the judicial officials to gather broad court discussion, translate the Ming Code in detail, consult the national system, add and subtract and measure, aiming at fairness.

units.zh: 書成奏進，朕再三覆閱，仍命內院諸臣校訂妥確，乃允刊布，名曰大清律集解附例。
units.en: When the book was completed and submitted, I reviewed it repeatedly, ordered the Inner Court ministers to collate it until correct, and then authorized its publication under the title Great Qing Code with Collected Exegesis and Attached Precedents.
units.literal: When the book was completed and submitted, I reviewed it again and again, still ordered the Inner Court ministers to collate it until correct, and then permitted its engraving and promulgation, naming it the Great Qing Code with Collected Exegesis and Attached Precedents.

units.zh: 爾內外有司官吏，敬此成憲，勿得任意低昂，務使百官萬民，畏名義而重犯法，冀幾刑措之風，以昭我祖宗好生之德。
units.en: You officials at court and in the provinces, revere this established code; do not arbitrarily raise or lower punishments. See that officials and common people alike fear disgrace and hold the law in awe, so that punishments may fall into disuse and our ancestors' virtue of cherishing life may be made manifest.
units.literal: You officials within and without, revere this established statute; do not arbitrarily raise or lower punishments. Endeavor to make the hundred officials and ten thousand people fear reputation and right conduct and regard violation of law as weighty, hoping for the wind of punishments set aside, to display our ancestors' virtue of cherishing life.

units.zh: 子孫臣民，其世世守之。」
units.en: Descendants and subjects, guard it generation after generation."
units.literal: Descendants and subjects, guard it generation after generation."

units.zh: 十三年，復頒滿文大清律。
units.en: In the thirteenth year the Great Qing Code in Manchu was promulgated again.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year the Great Qing Code in Manchu was again promulgated.

units.zh: 康熙九年，聖祖命大學士管理刑部尚書事對喀納等將律文復行校正。
units.en: In Kangxi 9 the Sacred Ancestor ordered Grand Secretary Duikana, who was acting as Minister of Punishments, and others to correct the statutory text once more.
units.literal: In the ninth year of Kangxi the Sacred Ancestor ordered Grand Secretary and acting Minister of Punishments Duikana and others again to correct the statutory text.

units.zh: 十八年，特諭刑部定律之外，所有條例，應去應存，著九卿、詹事、科道會同詳加酌定，確議具奏。
units.en: In the eighteenth year he specially instructed the Ministry of Punishments that, apart from the fixed code, all supplementary regulations—those to be removed and those to be kept—should be carefully deliberated jointly by the Nine Ministers, the Household Officials of the Heir Apparent, and the censorate, and reported in a definitive memorial.
units.literal: In the eighteenth year he specially instructed the Ministry of Punishments that apart from the fixed code, all supplementary regulations—those to be removed and those to be kept—should be deliberated in detail jointly by the Nine Ministers, the Household Officials of the Heir Apparent, and the censorate, with firm discussion submitted in memorial.

units.zh: 嗣經九卿等遵旨會同更改條例，別自為書，名為現行則例。
units.en: Subsequently the Nine Ministers and others, obeying the instruction, jointly revised the regulations and issued them as a separate book called the Current Precedents in Practice.
units.literal: Subsequently the Nine Ministers and others, obeying the instruction, jointly revised the regulations and set them apart as a separate book named the Current Precedents in Practice.

units.zh: 二十八年，台臣盛符升以律例須歸一貫，乞重加考定，以垂法守。
units.en: In the twenty-eighth year censor Sheng Fusheng argued that the code and precedents must be unified, and asked that they be re-examined and fixed so that a single standard of law might be handed down.
units.literal: In the twenty-eighth year censor Sheng Fusheng, on the grounds that code and precedents must be brought to unity, requested renewed examination and fixation so that legal observance might be handed down.

units.zh: 特交九卿議，准將現行則例附入大清律條。
units.en: The matter was referred to the Nine Ministers for discussion, and they approved attaching the Current Precedents in Practice to the articles of the Great Qing Code.
units.literal: The matter was specially referred to the Nine Ministers for discussion; approval was given to attach the Current Precedents in Practice to the articles of the Great Qing Code.

units.zh: 隨命大學士圖納、張玉書等為總裁。
units.en: Grand Secretaries Tuna, Zhang Yushu, and others were then appointed chief compilers.
units.literal: Grand Secretaries Tuna, Zhang Yushu, and others were then appointed chief compilers.

units.zh: 諸臣以律文昉自唐律，辭簡義賅，易致舛訛，於每篇正文後增用總注，疏解律義。
units.en: The ministers noted that the statutory text was modeled on the Tang Code: its language was concise and its meaning compressed, which easily led to error. They therefore added general annotations after the main text of each section to explain the meaning of the statutes.
units.literal: The ministers considered that the statutory text took its model from the Tang Code: the language was concise and the meaning compressed, easily leading to error; therefore after the main text of each section they added general annotations to explain the meaning of the statutes.

units.zh: 次第酌定名例四十六條，三十四年，先行繕呈。
units.en: They then worked through and fixed the forty-six articles of General Principles; in the thirty-fourth year these were first copied and submitted.
units.literal: In order they weighed and fixed the forty-six articles of General Principles; in the thirty-fourth year these were first copied and submitted.

units.zh: 三十六年，發回刑部，命將奏聞後更改之處補入。
units.en: In the thirty-sixth year it was sent back to the Ministry of Punishments with orders to insert the revisions made after the memorial was heard.
units.literal: In the thirty-sixth year it was sent back to the Ministry of Punishments with orders to insert the revisions made after the memorial was heard.

units.zh: 至四十六年六月，輯進四十二本，留覽未發。
units.en: By the sixth month of the forty-sixth year forty-two volumes were compiled and submitted; they were kept for imperial review and not issued.
units.literal: By the sixth month of the forty-sixth year forty-two volumes were compiled and submitted; they were retained for perusal and not issued.

units.zh: 雍正元年，巡視東城御史湯之旭奏：「律例最關緊要，今六部見行則例，或有從重改輕，從輕擬重，有先行而今停，事同而法異者，未經畫一。
units.en: In Yongzheng 1, Eastern Metropolitan censor Tang Zhixu memorialized: "The code and precedents are matters of the utmost importance. The currently enforced precedents of the Six Ministries sometimes change severity to leniency or leniency to severity; some were once enforced and are now suspended; the facts are the same but the law differs—they have not been unified.
units.literal: In the first year of Yongzheng, Eastern Metropolitan censor Tang Zhixu memorialized: "Code and precedents are matters of the utmost importance. The currently enforced precedents of the Six Ministries sometimes change severity to leniency or leniency to severity; some were enforced before and are stopped now; the facts are the same but the law differs—they have not been unified.

units.zh: 乞簡諳練律例大臣，專掌律例館總裁，將康熙六十一年以前之例並大清會典，逐條互訂，庶免參差。」
units.en: I ask that a minister skilled in code and precedents be selected to serve exclusively as chief compiler of the Code and Precedents Office, and that precedents before Kangxi 61 together with the Great Qing Statutes be checked article by article against one another, so that discrepancies may be avoided."
units.literal: I beg that a minister skilled in code and precedents be selected to take exclusive charge as chief compiler of the Code and Precedents Office, and that precedents before the sixty-first year of Kangxi together with the Great Qing Statutes be checked article by article against one another, so that discrepancies may be avoided."

units.zh: 世宗允之，命大學士硃軾等為總裁，諭令於應增應減之處，再行詳加分晰，作速修完。
units.en: The Shizong approved, appointed Grand Secretary Zhu Shi and others as chief compilers, and instructed that where additions and subtractions were needed they should be analyzed in detail and the revision completed swiftly.
units.literal: The Shizong approved, appointed Grand Secretary Zhu Shi and others as chief compilers, and instructed that where additions and subtractions were needed they should again be analyzed in detail and the revision completed swiftly.

units.zh: 三年書成，五年頒布。
units.en: The book was completed in the third year and promulgated in the fifth.
units.literal: In the third year the book was completed; in the fifth year it was promulgated.

units.zh: 蓋明律以名例居首，其次則分隸於六部，合計三十門，都凡四百六十條。
units.en: The Ming Code placed General Principles first; the statutes were then distributed under the Six Ministries, totaling thirty sections and four hundred sixty articles in all.
units.literal: The Ming Code placed General Principles first; next the statutes were distributed under the Six Ministries, totaling thirty sections and four hundred sixty articles in all.

units.zh: 順治初，釐定律書，將公式門之信牌移入職制，漏泄軍情移入軍政，於公式門刪漏用鈔印，於倉庫門刪鈔法，於詐偽門刪偽造寶鈔。
units.en: At the beginning of Shunzhi, when the law book was put in order, the section on credentials was moved from Administrative Forms to Official Regulations, and leaking military intelligence was moved into Military Administration; from Administrative Forms the article on omitting stamped documents was deleted, from Granaries the article on paper money was deleted, and from Fraud the article on forging treasure notes was deleted.
units.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi, when the law book was put in order, the section on credentials from the Administrative Forms chapter was moved into Official Regulations; leaking military intelligence was moved into Military Administration; from Administrative Forms the article on omitting to use stamped documents was deleted; from the Granaries chapter the article on paper money was deleted; from the Fraud chapter the article on forging treasure notes was deleted.

units.zh: 後又於名例增入邊遠充軍一條。
units.en: Later one article on military exile to remote regions was added to General Principles.
units.literal: Later one article on military exile to remote regions was added to General Principles.

units.zh: 雍正三年之律，其刪除者：名例律之吏卒犯死罪、殺害軍人、在京犯罪軍民共三條，職制門選用軍職、官吏給由二條，婚姻門之蒙古、色目人婚姻一條，宮衛門之懸帶關防牌面一條。
units.en: In the Yongzheng 3 code, the following were deleted: from General Principles three articles on clerks and runners guilty of capital crimes, killing soldiers, and military and civilian offenders in the capital; from Official Regulations two articles on selecting military posts and officials receiving credentials; from Marriage one article on Mongol and Semu marriages; and from Palace Guard one article on wearing pass tokens and seals.
units.literal: In the code of Yongzheng 3, what was deleted: from General Principles the three articles on clerks and runners guilty of capital crimes, killing soldiers, and military and civilian offenders in the capital; from Official Regulations the two articles on selecting military posts and officials receiving credentials; from Marriage the one article on Mongol and Semu marriages; from Palace Guard the one article on wearing pass tokens and seals.

units.zh: 其併入者：名例之邊遠充軍並於充軍地方，公式門之毀棄制書印信並二條為一，課程門之鹽法並十二條為一，宮衛門之衝突儀仗並三條為一，郵驛門之遞送公文並三條為一。
units.en: What was merged: remote military exile in General Principles was merged into the article on places of military exile; in Administrative Forms two articles on destroying imperial documents and seals were combined into one; in Revenue Duties twelve articles on salt law were combined into one; in Palace Guard three articles on clashing with ceremonial guards were combined into one; and in Postal Stations three articles on forwarding official documents were combined into one.
units.literal: What was merged: remote military exile in General Principles was merged into the article on places of military exile; in Administrative Forms the two articles on destroying imperial documents and seals were merged into one; in Revenue Duties the twelve articles on salt law were merged into one; in Palace Guard the three articles on clashing with ceremonial guards were merged into one; in Postal Stations the three articles on forwarding official documents were merged into one.

units.zh: 其改易者：名例之軍官軍人免發遣更為犯罪免發遣，軍官有犯更為軍籍有犯；
units.en: What was altered: in General Principles "military officers and soldiers exempt from banishment" was changed to "offenders exempt from banishment," and "officers who commit offenses" to "offenders registered in the military rolls";
units.literal: What was altered: in General Principles "military officers and soldiers exempt from banishment" was changed to "offenders exempt from banishment," and "officers who commit offenses" to "offenders registered in the military rolls";

units.zh: 儀制門之收藏禁書及私習天文生節為收藏禁書。
units.en: in Rites and Ceremonies the article on collecting forbidden books and privately studying astronomy was abridged to the article on collecting forbidden books alone.
units.literal: in Rites and Ceremonies the article on collecting forbidden books and privately studying astronomy was abridged to the article on collecting forbidden books.

units.zh: 其增入者：名例之天文生有犯充軍地方二條。
units.en: What was added: in General Principles two articles on astronomy students who offend and on places of military exile.
units.literal: What was added: in General Principles two articles on astronomy students who offend and places of military exile.

units.zh: 總計名例律四十六條。
units.en: In all, General Principles contained forty-six articles.
units.literal: In all, General Principles contained forty-six articles.

units.zh: 吏律：曰職制十四條，曰公式十四條。
units.en: Officials Code: Official Regulations, fourteen articles; Administrative Forms, fourteen articles.
units.literal: Officials Code: Official Regulations fourteen articles, Administrative Forms fourteen articles.

units.zh: 戶律：曰戶役十五條，曰田宅十一條，曰婚姻十七條，曰倉庫二十三條，曰課程八條，曰市廛五條。
units.en: Households Code: Household Service, fifteen articles; Fields and Dwellings, eleven; Marriage, seventeen; Granaries, twenty-three; Revenue Duties, eight; Markets, five.
units.literal: Households Code: Household Service fifteen articles, Fields and Dwellings eleven articles, Marriage seventeen articles, Granaries twenty-three articles, Revenue Duties eight articles, Markets five articles.

units.zh: 禮律：曰祭祀六條，曰儀制二十條。
units.en: Rites Code: Sacrifices, six articles; Rites and Ceremonies, twenty articles.
units.literal: Rites Code: Sacrifices six articles, Rites and Ceremonies twenty articles.

units.zh: 兵律：曰宮衛十六條，曰軍政二十一條，曰關津七條，曰廄牧十一條，曰郵驛十六條。
units.en: Military Code: Palace Guard, sixteen articles; Military Administration, twenty-one; Passes and Ferries, seven; Stables and Herds, eleven; Postal Stations, sixteen.
units.literal: Military Code: Palace Guard sixteen articles, Military Administration twenty-one articles, Passes and Ferries seven articles, Stables and Herds eleven articles, Postal Stations sixteen articles.

units.zh: 刑律：曰賊盜二十八條，曰人命二十條，曰鬥毆二十二條，曰罵詈八條，曰訴訟十二條，曰受贓十一條，曰詐偽十一條，曰犯奸十條，曰雜犯十一條，曰捕亡八條，曰斷獄二十九條。
units.en: Punishments Code: Robbery and Theft, twenty-eight articles; Homicide, twenty; Assault, twenty-two; Abuse, eight; Litigation, twelve; Accepting Bribes, eleven; Fraud, eleven; Sexual Offenses, ten; Miscellaneous Offenses, eleven; Apprehension of Fugitives, eight; Trial and Judgment, twenty-nine.
units.literal: Punishments Code: Robbery and Theft twenty-eight articles, Homicide twenty articles, Assault twenty-two articles, Abuse eight articles, Litigation twelve articles, Accepting Bribes eleven articles, Fraud eleven articles, Sexual Offenses ten articles, Miscellaneous Offenses eleven articles, Apprehension of Fugitives eight articles, Trial and Judgment twenty-nine articles.

units.zh: 工律：曰營造九條，曰河防四條。
units.en: Works Code: Construction, nine articles; River Control, four articles.
units.literal: Works Code: Construction nine articles, River Control four articles.

units.zh: 蓋仍明律三十門，而總為四百三十六條。
units.en: It still followed the Ming Code's thirty sections, but totaled four hundred thirty-six articles.
units.literal: Thus it still followed the Ming Code's thirty sections, but totaled four hundred thirty-six articles.

units.zh: 律首六贓圖、五刑圖、獄具圖、喪服圖，大都沿明之舊。
units.en: At the head of the code were diagrams of the six categories of bribery, the five punishments, prison implements, and mourning garments—mostly following the Ming as before.
units.literal: At the head of the code were diagrams of the six categories of bribery, the five punishments, prison implements, and mourning garments—mostly following the Ming as before.

units.zh: 納贖諸例圖、徒限內老疾收贖圖、誣輕為重收贖圖，銀數皆從現制。
units.en: Diagrams of commutation by payment, of the aged and infirm redeemed within the term of penal servitude, and of treating a light offense as heavy for redemption—all silver amounts followed the current system.
units.literal: Diagrams of commutation by payment, of the aged and infirm redeemed within the term of penal servitude, and of treating light error as heavy for redemption—all silver amounts followed the current system.

units.zh: 其律文及律注，頗有增損改易。
units.en: The statutory text and annotations underwent considerable additions, deletions, and revisions.
units.literal: The statutory text and statutory annotations had considerable additions, subtractions, and alterations.

units.zh: 律後總注，則康熙年間所創造。
units.en: The general annotations after the statutes were a Kangxi-era innovation.
units.literal: The general annotations after the statutes were a creation of the Kangxi period.

units.zh: 律末並附比引律三十條。
units.en: At the end of the code were also attached thirty articles of analogous citation statutes.
units.literal: At the end of the code were also attached thirty articles of analogous citation statutes.

units.zh: 此其大較也。
units.en: Such was the general outline.
units.literal: This is the general outline.

units.zh: 自時厥後，雖屢經纂修，然僅續增附律之條例，而律文未之或改。
units.en: From that time onward, although the code was revised repeatedly, only the supplementary precedents were continually added; the statutory text itself was never changed.
units.literal: From that time onward, although there were repeated compilations and revisions, only the supplementary precedents attached to the code were continually added; the statutory text itself was never altered.

units.zh: 惟乾隆五年，館修奏准芟除總注，並補入過失殺傷收贖一圖而已。
units.en: Only in Qianlong 5 did the compiling office obtain approval to remove the general annotations and add one diagram on redemption for negligent killing and wounding—and that alone.
units.literal: Only in the fifth year of Qianlong did the compiling office memorialize approval to cut away the general annotations and add one diagram on redemption for negligent killing and wounding—that alone.

units.zh: 例文自康熙初年僅存三百二十一條，末年增一百一十五條。
units.en: As for precedent texts, at the beginning of Kangxi only three hundred twenty-one articles remained; by the end of the reign one hundred fifteen more were added.
units.literal: As for precedent texts, at the beginning of Kangxi only three hundred twenty-one articles remained; by the end of the reign one hundred fifteen were added.

units.zh: 雍正三年，分別訂定，曰原例，累朝舊例凡三百二十一條；
units.en: In Yongzheng 3 they were separately fixed and designated: Original Precedents, old precedents of successive reigns totaling three hundred twenty-one articles;
units.literal: In Yongzheng 3 they were separately fixed and designated: Original Precedents, old precedents of successive reigns totaling three hundred twenty-one articles;

units.zh: 曰增例，康熙間現行例凡二百九十條；
units.en: Added Precedents, currently enforced precedents of the Kangxi period totaling two hundred ninety articles;
units.literal: Added Precedents, currently enforced precedents of the Kangxi period totaling two hundred ninety articles;

units.zh: 曰欽定例，上諭及臣工條奏凡二百有四條，總計八百十有五條。
units.en: Imperially Fixed Precedents, imperial instructions and ministers' submitted articles totaling two hundred four articles—in all eight hundred fifteen articles.
units.literal: Imperially Fixed Precedents, imperial instructions and ministers' submitted articles totaling two hundred four articles—in all eight hundred fifteen articles.

units.zh: 其立法之善者，如犯罪存留養親，推及孀婦獨子；
units.en: Among the sound provisions of legislation were such measures as allowing offenders to remain at home to support their parents, extended to widows with only sons;
units.literal: Among the good points of legislation were such provisions as allowing offenders to remain at home to support their parents, extended to widows with only sons;

units.zh: 若毆兄致死，並得准其承祀，恤孤嫠且教孝也。
units.en: if one beat an elder brother to death, one might still be permitted to continue the sacrifices—showing compassion for the solitary and widowed while teaching filial piety.
units.literal: if one beat an elder brother to death, one might still be permitted to continue the sacrifices—showing compassion for the solitary and widowed and teaching filial piety.

units.zh: 犯死罪非常赦所不原，察有祖父子孫陣亡，准其優免一次，勸忠也。
units.en: For capital crimes not normally pardoned by general amnesty, if investigation found that grandfathers, fathers, or sons had died in battle, one special mitigation was permitted—encouraging loyalty.
units.literal: For capital crimes not normally pardoned by general amnesty, if investigation found grandfathers, fathers, or sons who died in battle, one special mitigation was permitted—encouraging loyalty.

units.zh: 枉法贓有祿人八十兩，無祿人及不枉法贓有祿人一百二十兩，俱實絞，嚴貪墨之誅也。
units.en: For bribes taken by twisting the law, salaried officials at eighty taels; for unsalaried persons and for non-twisting bribes by salaried officials, one hundred twenty taels—all were executed by strangulation in fact, strictly punishing corruption.
units.literal: For bribes taken by twisting the law, salaried officials at eighty taels, unsalaried persons and non-twisting bribes by salaried officials at one hundred twenty taels—all were executed by strangulation in fact, strictly punishing corruption.

units.zh: 衙蠹索詐，驗贓加等治罪，懲胥役所以保良懦也。
units.en: Yamen parasites who extorted and swindled, once the bribe was verified, were punished by increased grades—punishing clerks and runners in order to protect the honest and defenseless.
units.literal: Yamen parasites who extorted and swindled, once the bribe was verified, were punished by increased grades—punishing clerks and runners in order to protect the good and timid.

units.zh: 強盜分別法無可貸、情有可原，殲渠魁、赦脅從之義也。
units.en: Robbers were distinguished between those whom the law could not spare and those with excusable circumstances—exterminating ringleaders while pardoning the coerced.
units.literal: Robbers were distinguished between those the law could not spare and those with excusable circumstances—exterminating ringleaders and pardoning the coerced.

units.zh: 復仇以國法得伸與否為斷，杜兇殘之路也。
units.en: Vengeance was decided by whether the national law could be fulfilled or not—blocking the path of cruel violence.
units.literal: Vengeance was decided by whether the national law could be fulfilled or not—blocking the path of cruel violence.

units.zh: 凡此諸端，或隱合古義，或矯正前失，皆良法也。
units.en: All these provisions either tacitly accorded with ancient principle or corrected previous errors—all were sound laws.
units.literal: All these points either tacitly accorded with ancient meaning or corrected previous errors—all were good laws.

units.zh: 而要皆定制於康、雍時。
units.en: Yet the essentials were all established in the Kangxi and Yongzheng periods.
units.literal: Yet the essentials were all fixed in the Kangxi and Yongzheng periods.

units.zh: 又國初以來，凡纂修律例，類必欽命二三大臣為總裁，特開專館。
units.en: Moreover, from the founding of the state, whenever the code and precedents were compiled and revised, two or three great ministers were invariably appointed by imperial command as chief compilers, and a special office was opened.
units.literal: Moreover, from the founding of the state, whenever code and precedents were compiled and revised, two or three great ministers were invariably appointed by imperial command as chief compilers, and a special office was opened.

units.zh: 維時各部院則例陸續成書，苟與刑律相涉，館員俱一一釐正，故鮮乖牾。
units.en: At that time the precedents of the various ministries and courts were completed one after another; whenever they touched on penal statutes, the office members corrected them one by one, so conflicts were rare.
units.literal: At that time the precedents of the various ministries and courts were completed one after another; if they touched on penal statutes, the office members all corrected them one by one, so there was rarely conflict.

units.zh: 自乾隆元年，刑部奏准三年修例一次。
units.en: From Qianlong 1 the Ministry of Punishments obtained approval to revise precedents once every three years.
units.literal: From the first year of Qianlong the Ministry of Punishments memorialized approval to revise precedents once every three years.

units.zh: 十一年，內閣等衙門議改五年一修。
units.en: In the eleventh year the Inner Court and other offices deliberated changing this to revision once every five years.
units.literal: In the eleventh year the Inner Court and other offices deliberated changing this to revision once every five years.

units.zh: 由是刑部專司其事，不復簡派總裁，律例館亦遂附屬於刑曹，與他部往往不相關會。
units.en: Thereupon the Ministry of Punishments took exclusive charge of the matter; chief compilers were no longer specially appointed, and the Code and Precedents Office was attached to the penal bureaucracy, often without coordination with other ministries.
units.literal: Thereupon the Ministry of Punishments took exclusive charge of the matter; chief compilers were no longer specially appointed, and the Code and Precedents Office was thus attached to the penal bureaucracy, often without coordination with other ministries.

units.zh: 高宗臨御六十年，性矜明察，每閱讞牘，必求其情罪曲當，以萬變不齊之情，欲御以萬變不齊之例。
units.en: The Qianlong Emperor reigned for sixty years. By nature meticulous and keenly discerning, he scrutinized every criminal case that came before him, insisting that the facts and the sentence fit together justly. He sought to meet the infinite variety of human circumstances with an equally varied body of legal precedent.
units.literal: The High Emperor reigned for sixty years. By nature he was proud and keenly perceptive. Whenever he reviewed criminal dossiers, he always sought whether the facts and the punishment were properly matched. He wished to govern circumstances that varied in ten thousand ways with precedents that likewise varied in ten thousand ways.

units.zh: 故乾隆一朝纂修八九次，刪原例、增例諸名目，而改變舊例及因案增設者為獨多。
units.en: During the Qianlong reign the code was therefore compiled and revised eight or nine times. Revisions took many forms—deleting original precedents, adding new ones, altering old rules, and creating precedents in response to individual cases—but changes to existing precedents and case-driven additions were by far the most common.
units.literal: Therefore, in the Qianlong reign the code was compiled and revised eight or nine times. Under such headings as deleted original precedents and added precedents, changes to old precedents and precedents added because of cases were especially numerous.

units.zh: 嘉慶以降，按期開館，沿道光、咸豐以迄同治，而條例乃增至一千八百九十有二。
units.en: From the Jiaqing reign onward, compilation offices opened at regular intervals, continuing through Daoguang and Xianfeng into Tongzhi, until the body of precedents swelled to 1,892 articles.
units.literal: From the Jiaqing reign onward, offices were opened on schedule, continuing through Daoguang and Xianfeng down to Tongzhi, and the articles of precedent eventually increased to one thousand eight hundred and ninety-two.

units.zh: 蓋清代定例，一如宋時之編敕，有例不用律，律既多成虛文，而例遂愈滋繁碎。
units.en: In essence, the Qing practice of codifying precedent resembled the Song dynasty's compilation of edicts: when a precedent applied, the statute did not. As the statutes themselves largely became dead letter, precedent grew ever more fragmented and prolix.
units.literal: In general, the Qing establishment of precedents was just like the Song compilation of edicts: where precedents existed, the statutes were not used. Since the statutes largely became empty words on paper, the precedents grew ever more fragmented and numerous.

units.zh: 其間前後牴觸，或律外加重，或因例破律，或一事設一例，或一省一地方專一例，甚且因此例而生彼例，不惟與他部則例參差，即一例分載各門者，亦不無歧異。
units.en: These provisions often contradicted one another. Some imposed penalties harsher than the statutes allowed; others overrode the statutes entirely through precedent. A single case might spawn its own rule; a single province or locality might receive a rule of its own. One precedent might even beget another. The result was inconsistency not only with regulations in other ministries, but also internal disagreement when the same precedent was recorded under different sections of the code.
units.literal: Among them, some contradicted one another from beginning to end; some imposed penalties beyond what the statutes allowed; some broke the statutes through precedent; some established one precedent for one matter, or one special precedent for one province or one locality; some even gave rise to one precedent from another. Not only did they fail to align with the regulations of other ministries—even when a single precedent was divided and recorded under different sections, discrepancies were not lacking.

units.zh: 展轉糾紛，易滋高下。
units.en: Disputes multiplied and entangled with one another, making arbitrary and uneven enforcement all too easy.
units.literal: As disputes wound on and on, unevenness in application was easily bred.

units.zh: 雍正十三年，世宗遺詔有曰：「國家刑罰禁令之設，所以詰奸除暴，懲貪黜邪，以端風俗，以肅官方者也。
units.en: In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng, the Yongzheng Emperor's deathbed edict declared: "The state establishes punishments and prohibitions to root out wickedness and violence, punish greed and drive out corruption, rectify public morals, and keep officialdom in order.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongzheng, the late Emperor Shizong's testamentary edict stated: "The establishment of the state's punishments, prohibitions, and bans is meant to interrogate the wicked and eliminate violence, punish greed and dismiss the corrupt, to rectify customs and to awe officialdom.

units.zh: 然寬嚴之用，又必因乎其時。
units.en: Yet whether to apply the law leniently or severely must always depend on the times.
units.literal: Yet the application of leniency and severity must also accord with the times.

units.zh: 從前朕見人情淺薄，官吏營私，相習成風，罔知省改，不得不懲治整理，以戒將來。
units.en: In the past I saw that public morals had grown shallow, that officials pursued private gain until corruption had become habit, and that none knew how to restrain themselves or reform. I had no choice but to punish and set things in order, so as to warn those who would come after.
units.literal: Previously I saw that human sentiment was shallow and base, that officials pursued private gain until it became custom, knowing no restraint or reform. I had no choice but to punish and rectify, to warn the future.

units.zh: 今人心共知警惕矣，凡各衙門條例，有前嚴而改寬者，此乃從前部臣定議未協，朕與廷臣悉心酌核而後更定，自可垂諸永久。
units.en: Now everyone knows to be on guard. Where regulations in the various yamens were once strict and have been relaxed, this is because the ministries' earlier deliberations had not been sound. After the court ministers and I examined them carefully and revised them, such changes may stand permanently.
units.literal: Now all hearts alike know to be on guard. Among the regulations of each yamen, those that were formerly strict and were changed to lenient—this was because the previous deliberations of ministerial officials were not harmonious. After I and the court ministers carefully weighed and revised them, they can naturally endure forever.

units.zh: 若前寬而改嚴者，此乃整飭人心風俗之計，原欲暫行於一時，俟諸弊革除，仍可酌復舊章，此朕本意也。
units.en: Where rules once lenient were made strict, that was a measure to discipline public morals and reform custom, originally meant to be temporary. Once the abuses had been removed, the old regulations could be restored as appropriate. That was my original intent.
units.literal: If those formerly lenient were changed to strict—this was a plan to discipline the hearts of the people and correct customs, originally intended to be applied temporarily for a time. Once the various abuses were eliminated, the old regulations could still be restored at discretion. This was my original intent.

units.zh: 向後遇事斟酌，如有應從舊例者，仍照舊例行。」
units.en: Henceforth, when cases arise, weigh each matter on its merits. Where the old precedents should apply, follow the old precedents.'
units.literal: Going forward, when matters arise, deliberate as needed. If old precedents should be followed, still act according to the old precedents.'

units.zh: 惜後世議法諸臣，未盡明世輕世重之故，每屆修例，第將歷奉諭旨及議准臣工條奏節次編入，從未統合全書，逐條釐正。
units.en: Alas, the ministers who debated law in later generations never fully grasped why penalties should be lighter in one age and heavier in another. At each revision they merely appended, in chronological order, the edicts previously received and the memorials approved by the bureaucracy. They never consolidated the whole corpus and corrected it provision by provision.
units.literal: Alas, the ministers who deliberated on law in later generations did not fully understand the reasons for lighter penalties in one age and heavier penalties in another. Each time precedents were revised, they merely compiled in sequence the imperial edicts received over time and the memorials submitted and approved by officials, never synthesizing the entire book and correcting it article by article.

units.zh: 穆宗號稱中興，母后柄政，削平發、捻、回疆之亂，百端待理，尚於同治九年纂修一次。
units.en: Emperor Tongzhi was hailed as restoring the dynasty. With the Empress Dowager holding power and the Taiping, Nian, and Muslim frontier rebellions newly suppressed, the court faced a hundred pressing tasks—yet in the ninth year of Tongzhi it still undertook one full revision of the code.
units.literal: Emperor Muzong was hailed as restoring the dynasty. The Empress Dowager held power. The Taiping, Nian, and Muslim frontier rebellions were suppressed. Though a hundred matters awaited attention, still in the ninth year of Tongzhi the code was compiled and revised once.

units.zh: 德宗幼沖繼統，未遑興作。
units.en: The Guangxu Emperor succeeded the throne while still a child and had no opportunity to launch such projects.
units.literal: Emperor Dezong succeeded the throne while still young and had no leisure for such undertakings.

units.zh: 兼之時勢多故，章程叢積，刑部既憚其繁猥，不敢議修，群臣亦未有言及者，因循久之。
units.en: The times were also unsettled, and regulations accumulated in overwhelming numbers. The Board of Punishments, intimidated by the sheer bulk and complexity of the material, dared not propose a revision, and no minister raised the matter. Inertia therefore persisted for years.
units.literal: Moreover the times were troubled, regulations piled up in profusion. The Board of Punishments already feared their tedium and complexity and dared not propose revision, and no minister spoke of it either. Thus delay went on for a long time.

units.zh: 逮光緒二十六年，聯軍入京，兩宮西狩。
units.en: By the twenty-sixth year of Guangxu, the allied armies entered Beijing and the two sovereigns fled west.
units.literal: By the twenty-sixth year of Guangxu, the allied armies entered the capital and both sovereigns fled west.

units.zh: 憂時之士，咸謂非取法歐、美，不足以圖強。
units.en: Men anxious for the fate of the realm agreed that China could not become strong unless it learned from Europe and America.
units.literal: Men concerned for the times all said that unless they took Europe and America as models, it would not suffice to pursue national strength.

units.zh: 於是條陳時事者，頗稍稍議及刑律。
units.en: Memorialists on current affairs then began, little by little, to touch upon criminal law as well.
units.literal: Thereupon those who memorialized on current affairs began, little by little, to discuss criminal law as well.

units.zh: 二十八年，直隸總督袁世凱、兩江總督劉坤一、湖廣總督張之洞，會保刑部左侍郎沈家本、出使美國大臣伍廷芳修訂法律，兼取中西。
units.en: In the twenty-eighth year, Viceroy Yuan Shikai of Zhili, Viceroy Liu Kunyi of Liangjiang, and Viceroy Zhang Zhidong of Huguang jointly recommended Left Vice Minister of Punishments Shen Jiaben and Minister to the United States Wu Tingfang to revise the laws, combining Chinese and Western approaches.
units.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, the Viceroy of Zhili Yuan Shikai, the Viceroy of Liangjiang Liu Kunyi, and the Viceroy of Huguang Zhang Zhidong jointly recommended the Left Vice Minister of Punishments Shen Jiaben and the Minister Plenipotentiary to the United States Wu Tingfang to revise the laws, drawing on both Chinese and Western sources.

units.zh: 旨如所請，並諭將一切現行律例，按照通商交涉情形，參酌各國法律，妥為擬議，務期中外通行，有裨治理。
units.en: The throne approved the request and further ordered that all current statutes and precedents be reconsidered in light of treaty and commercial relations, with reference to foreign legal systems, and carefully redrafted so that the law might serve both domestic and international needs and strengthen governance.
units.literal: An edict approved the request and further instructed that all current statutes and precedents be, in accordance with commercial and diplomatic circumstances, deliberated upon with reference to the laws of various countries, properly drafted, with the aim that they would prevail both within and without China and benefit governance.

units.zh: 自此而議律者，乃群措意於領事裁判權。
units.en: From this time onward, those debating legal reform focused above all on consular jurisdiction.
units.literal: From this point those who discussed law collectively turned their attention to consular jurisdiction.

units.zh: 是年刑部亦奏請開館修例。
units.en: That same year the Board of Punishments also memorialized asking permission to open an office for revising precedents.
units.literal: That same year the Board of Punishments also memorialized requesting to open an office to revise precedents.

units.zh: 三十一年，先將例內今昔情形不同，及例文無關引用，或兩例重複，或舊例停止者，奏准刪除三百四十四條。
units.en: In the thirty-first year, the court first approved the deletion of 344 precedents whose circumstances had changed, whose wording was no longer applicable, that duplicated other provisions, or that had already fallen into disuse.
units.literal: In the thirty-first year, memorial approval was first granted to delete three hundred and forty-four articles—those precedents whose present and past circumstances differed, whose text was irrelevant to application, where two precedents duplicated each other, or where old precedents had been suspended.

units.zh: 三十三年，更命侍郎俞廉三與沈家本俱充修訂法律大臣。
units.en: In the thirty-third year, Vice Minister Yu Liansan was appointed together with Shen Jiaben as commissioners for legal revision.
units.literal: In the thirty-third year, Vice Minister Yu Liansan was further appointed together with Shen Jiaben as Commissioners for Revising the Laws.

units.zh: 沈家本等乃徵集館員，分科纂輯，並延聘東西各國之博士律師，藉備顧問。
units.en: Shen Jiaben and his colleagues then assembled a staff, divided the work by subject, and retained legal scholars and practicing lawyers from East and West as advisers.
units.literal: Shen Jiaben and the others then gathered staff members, organized compilation by subject, and engaged doctors of law and lawyers from Eastern and Western countries as consultants.

units.zh: 其前數年編纂未竣之舊律，亦特設編案處，歸併分修。
units.en: For older legal projects left unfinished in earlier years, they also set up a special drafting office to consolidate the materials and divide the remaining work.
units.literal: For the old statutes whose compilation in previous years had not been completed, a special drafting office was also established to consolidate and divide the work of revision.

units.zh: 十二月，遵旨議定滿、漢通行刑律，又刪並舊例四十九條。
units.en: In the twelfth month, pursuant to imperial instruction, they finalized a criminal code applicable to both Manchu and Han subjects and deleted or merged forty-nine obsolete precedents.
units.literal: In the twelfth month, following the edict they deliberated and settled the criminal code applicable to both Manchu and Han, and further deleted and merged forty-nine old precedents.

units.zh: 宣統元年，全書纂成繕進，諭交憲政編查館核議。
units.en: In the first year of Xuantong, when the completed work was compiled and presented to the throne, an edict ordered it sent to the Constitutional Drafting and Review Office for examination.
units.literal: In the first year of Xuantong, when the complete work was compiled and submitted, an edict ordered it transmitted to the Constitutional Drafting and Review Office for examination and deliberation.

units.zh: 二年，覆奏訂定，名為現行刑律。
units.en: In the second year, after further review and confirmation, it was given the title Current Criminal Code.
units.literal: In the second year, upon resubmission it was fixed and named the Current Criminal Code.

units.zh: 時官制改變，立憲詔下，東西洋學說朋興。
units.en: At that time the official system was being reformed, constitutional edicts were issued, and Eastern and Western doctrines flourished side by side.
units.literal: At that time the official system was changing, constitutional edicts were issued, and Eastern and Western doctrines flourished together.

units.zh: 律雖仍舊分三十門，而芟削六部之目。
units.en: Although the code still kept the old division into thirty sections, the categories tied to the Six Ministries were cut away.
units.literal: Although the code still followed the old division into thirty sections, the headings of the Six Ministries were pruned away.

units.zh: 其因時事推移及新章遞嬗而刪者，如名例之犯罪免發遣、軍籍有犯、流囚家屬、流犯在道會赦、天文生有犯、工樂戶及婦人犯罪、充軍地方，職制之大臣專擅選官、文官不許封公侯、官員赴任過限、無故不朝參公座、奸黨，公式之照刷文卷、磨勘卷宗、封掌印信，戶役之丁夫差遣不平、隱蔽差役、逃避差役，田宅之任所置買田宅，婚姻之同姓為婚、良賤為婚姻，課程之監臨勢要中鹽、阻壞鹽法、私礬、舶商匿貨，禮制之朝見留難，宮衛之內府工作人匠替役，軍政之邊境申索軍需、公侯私役官軍、夜禁，關津之私越冒度關津、詐冒給路引、遞送逃軍妻女出城、私出外境及違禁下海、私役弓兵，廄牧之公使人等索借馬匹，郵驛之占宿驛舍上房，賊盜之起除刺字，鬥毆之良賤相毆，訴訟之軍民約會、詞訟誣告、充軍及遷徙，受贓之私受公侯財物，犯奸之良賤相奸，雜犯之搬做雜劇，捕亡之徒流人逃，斷獄之徒囚不應役，營造之有司官吏不住公廨是也。
units.en: Articles removed as events moved on and new rules replaced old ones included, among others: under General Principles, crimes exempt from exile, offenses by persons on military registers, families of transported convicts, transported offenders meeting amnesty en route, offenses by astronomy students, crimes by artisan-musician households and by women, and places of military exile; under Official Regulations, grand ministers arrogating the selection of officials, civil officials barred from enfeoffment as duke or marquis, officials exceeding the deadline for taking up a post, absenting oneself from court without cause, and factional cliques; under Administrative Forms, auditing documents, scrutinizing case files, and sealing and keeping official seals; under Household Service, unfair dispatch of corvée laborers, concealing corvée service, and evading corvée service; under Fields and Dwellings, purchasing fields and dwellings at one's post; under Marriage, marriage within the same surname and marriage between commoners and debased persons; under Revenue Duties, powerful officials monopolizing salt, obstructing the salt law, private alum, and merchant ships concealing goods; under Rites and Ceremonies, obstructing audiences; under Palace Guard, substitute service for inner-palace artisan laborers; under Military Administration, border regions demanding military supplies, dukes and marquises privately employing official troops, and the night curfew; under Passes and Ferries, privately crossing or falsely passing checkpoints, fraudulently obtaining travel permits, escorting fugitive soldiers' wives and daughters out of the city, privately leaving the border or violating prohibitions by going to sea, and privately employing archer-soldiers; under Stables and Herds, envoys and the like demanding or borrowing horses; under Postal Stations, occupying upper rooms at relay stations; under Robbery and Theft, removing tattoo marks; under Assault, mutual assault between commoners and debased persons; under Litigation, military and civilian gatherings, false accusation in lawsuits, and military exile and relocation; under Accepting Bribes, privately accepting goods from dukes and marquises; under Sexual Offenses, adultery between commoners and debased persons; under Miscellaneous Offenses, performing miscellaneous plays; under Apprehension of Fugitives, penal servitude and exile offenders fleeing; under Trial and Judgment, penal servitude prisoners refusing labor; and under Construction, responsible officials not residing at government offices.
units.literal: Those deleted because current affairs shifted and new statutes succeeded one another included, among others: under General Principles, crimes exempt from exile, offenses by persons on military registers, families of transported convicts, transported offenders meeting amnesty en route, offenses by astronomy students, crimes by artisan-musician households and by women, and places of military exile; under Official Regulations, grand ministers arrogating the selection of officials, civil officials barred from enfeoffment as duke or marquis, officials exceeding the deadline for taking up a post, absenting oneself from court without cause, and factional cliques; under Administrative Forms, auditing documents, scrutinizing case files, and sealing and keeping official seals; under Household Service, unfair dispatch of corvée laborers, concealing corvée service, and evading corvée service; under Fields and Dwellings, purchasing fields and dwellings at one's post; under Marriage, marriage within the same surname and marriage between commoners and debased persons; under Revenue Duties, powerful officials monopolizing salt, obstructing the salt law, private alum, and merchant ships concealing goods; under Rites and Ceremonies, obstructing audiences; under Palace Guard, substitute service for inner-palace artisan laborers; under Military Administration, border regions demanding military supplies, dukes and marquises privately employing official troops, and the night curfew; under Passes and Ferries, privately crossing or falsely passing checkpoints, fraudulently obtaining travel permits, escorting fugitive soldiers' wives and daughters out of the city, privately leaving the border or violating prohibitions by going to sea, and privately employing archer-soldiers; under Stables and Herds, envoys and the like demanding or borrowing horses; under Postal Stations, occupying upper rooms at relay stations; under Robbery and Theft, removing tattoo marks; under Assault, mutual assault between commoners and debased persons; under Litigation, military and civilian gatherings, false accusation in lawsuits, and military exile and relocation; under Accepting Bribes, privately accepting goods from dukes and marquises; under Sexual Offenses, adultery between commoners and debased persons; under Miscellaneous Offenses, performing miscellaneous plays; under Apprehension of Fugitives, penal servitude and exile offenders fleeing; under Trial and Judgment, penal servitude prisoners refusing labor; and under Construction, responsible officials not residing at government offices.

units.zh: 其緣政體及刑制遷變而改者，如名例之化外人有犯改為蒙古及入國籍人有犯，徒流遷徙地方改為五徒三流二遣地方，婚姻之娶樂人為妻妾改娶娼妓為妻，人命之殺子孫及奴婢圖賴人節去「及奴婢」字，鬥毆之奴婢毆家長改為僱工人毆家長，罵詈之奴婢罵家長改為僱工人罵家長，犯奸之奴婢奸家長妻改為僱工人奸家長妻是也。
units.en: Articles revised because the political and penal systems changed included, among others: under General Principles, "Offenses by Aliens" became "Offenses by Mongols" and "Offenses by Naturalized Persons"; places for penal servitude, exile, and relocation became places for the five degrees of penal servitude, three degrees of exile, and two degrees of banishment; under Marriage, "taking female entertainers as wives and concubines" became "taking prostitutes as wives"; under Homicide, the words "and bondservants" were cut from the article on killing descendants and bondservants to extort through false accusation; under Assault, "bondservants assaulting the head of household" became "hired laborers assaulting the head of household"; under Abuse, "bondservants abusing the head of household" became "hired laborers abusing the head of household"; and under Sexual Offenses, "bondservants committing adultery with the head of household's wife" became "hired laborers committing adultery with the head of household's wife."
units.literal: Those changed because the political system and penal system shifted included, among others: under General Principles, "Offenses by Aliens" became "Offenses by Mongols" and "Offenses by Naturalized Persons"; places for penal servitude, exile, and relocation became places for the five degrees of penal servitude, three degrees of exile, and two degrees of banishment; under Marriage, "taking female entertainers as wives and concubines" became "taking prostitutes as wives"; under Homicide, the words "and bondservants" were cut from the article on killing descendants and bondservants to extort through false accusation; under Assault, "bondservants assaulting the head of household" became "hired laborers assaulting the head of household"; under Abuse, "bondservants abusing the head of household" became "hired laborers abusing the head of household"; and under Sexual Offenses, "bondservants committing adultery with the head of household's wife" became "hired laborers committing adultery with the head of household's wife."

units.zh: 綜計全律仍存三百八十有九條，而比引律則刪存及半，依類散入各門，不列比附之目。
units.en: In all, the code still contained three hundred eighty-nine articles; the analogous citation statutes were reduced to about half, distributed by category among the various sections, and no longer listed under a separate heading for analogical application.
units.literal: Taking the code as a whole, three hundred eighty-nine articles still remained; the analogous citation statutes were cut to about half, scattered by category into the various sections, with no separate catalog of analogical application.

units.zh: 舊例除刪並外，合續纂之新例，統一千六十六條。
units.en: Apart from deletions and mergers among old precedents, the newly compiled precedents brought the total to one thousand sixty-six articles.
units.literal: Apart from deletions and mergers among old precedents, together with newly compiled precedents, there were in all one thousand sixty-six articles.

units.zh: 其督捕則例一書，順治朝命臣工纂進，原為旗下逃奴而設。
units.en: As for the Regulations for Supervision and Apprehension, the Shunzhi court ordered officials to compile and submit them; they had originally been devised for fugitive Banner slaves.
units.literal: As for the book of Regulations for Supervision and Apprehension, the Shunzhi court ordered officials to compile and submit it; it was originally established for Banner fugitive slaves.

units.zh: 康熙十五年重加酌定，乾隆以後續有增入，計條文一百一十，亦經分別去留，附入刑律，而全書悉廢。
units.en: In Kangxi 15 it was reexamined and revised; after Qianlong further additions were made, bringing the total to one hundred ten articles; these too were selectively kept or discarded, incorporated into the penal code, and the entire book was abolished.
units.literal: In Kangxi 15 it was reexamined and fixed; after Qianlong additions continued, totaling one hundred ten articles; these too were selectively retained or removed, attached to the penal code, and the entire book was abolished.

units.zh: 律首仍載服制全圖，以重禮教。
units.en: The complete diagram of mourning garments was still placed at the head of the code, to emphasize ritual instruction.
units.literal: At the head of the code the complete diagram of mourning garments was still included, to emphasize ritual instruction.

units.zh: 是年冬頒行焉。
units.en: It was promulgated that winter.
units.literal: That winter it was promulgated.

units.zh: 若蒙古治罪各條，載諸理籓院則例，及西寧番子治罪條例，別行諸岷、洮等處者，以其習俗既殊，刑制亦異，未敢輕議更張。
units.en: As for the various articles on punishing Mongols, recorded in the precedents of the Court of Colonial Affairs, and the regulations on punishing Xining frontier peoples separately enforced in Min, Tao, and other regions—their customs were already different and their penal systems differed as well, so no one dared lightly propose a thorough overhaul.
units.literal: As for the various articles on punishing Mongols, recorded in the precedents of the Court of Colonial Affairs, and the regulations on punishing Xining frontier peoples separately enforced in Min, Tao, and other regions—because their customs were already different and their penal systems also differed, no one dared lightly propose fundamental change.

units.zh: 新律則光緒三十二年法律館撰上刑民訴訟律，酌取英、美陪審制度。
units.en: As for the new code, in Guangxu 32 the Law Compilation Office drafted and submitted the Criminal and Civil Procedure Code, selectively adopting British and American jury systems.
units.literal: As for the new code, in Guangxu 32 the Law Compilation Office drafted and submitted the Criminal and Civil Procedure Code, drawing selectively on British and American jury systems.

units.zh: 各督撫多議其窒礙，遂寢。
units.en: Various governors-general and governors mostly argued that it was impracticable, and the project was shelved.
units.literal: Various governors-general and governors mostly argued that it was obstructive, and so it was shelved.

units.zh: 三十三年，復先後奏上新刑律草案，總則十七章：曰法例，曰不論罪，曰未遂罪，曰累犯罪，曰俱發罪，曰共犯罪，曰刑名，曰宥恕減輕，曰自首減免，曰酌量減輕，曰加減例，曰緩刑，曰暫釋，曰恩赦，曰時效，曰時期計算，曰文例。
units.en: In year 33 they again submitted the draft New Penal Code in succession, with seventeen chapters of General Provisions: Legal Examples; Crimes Not Punishable; Attempted Crimes; Repeated Crimes; Concurrent Crimes; Joint Crimes; Names of Punishments; Pardon and Mitigation; Mitigation for Voluntary Surrender; Discretionary Mitigation; Rules for Increase and Decrease; Suspended Sentences; Temporary Release; Gracious Amnesty; Statute of Limitations; Calculation of Time Periods; and Textual Rules.
units.literal: In year 33 they again memorialized in succession submitting the draft New Penal Code, with seventeen chapters of General Provisions: Legal Examples, Crimes Not Punishable, Attempted Crimes, Repeated Crimes, Concurrent Crimes, Joint Crimes, Names of Punishments, Pardon and Mitigation, Mitigation for Voluntary Surrender, Discretionary Mitigation, Rules for Increase and Decrease, Suspended Sentences, Temporary Release, Gracious Amnesty, Statute of Limitations, Calculation of Time Periods, and Textual Rules.

units.literal: The two parts together totaled three hundred eighty-seven articles; after the Constitutional Research Bureau memorialized submitting them to ministries, courts, and frontier officials for review, those who annotated objections were many.
